Every record, count, price, area and verification note shown here is read from data/public_inventory.js, copied from production on 11 November 2026. Nothing is invented for this study. Photographs are labelled representative because that is how the source data labels all 347 of them.

Bench A · empty search results

A search that returns nothing

Seeded with a real filter combination that genuinely matches zero of the 347 records. The drawing explains the shape of the problem; the copy and the counts give the way out. Active filters survive, each removable on its own, each showing what it would cost to keep.

Bench B · saved properties, nothing saved

Before anything is saved

Saving does not exist in production yet, so this empty state has a second job: it has to teach what saving is for. The brief asks for something beyond a bookmark icon — here the drawing is the comparison itself, three bays of a register with nothing set out in them.

0 saved · the index above writes here

Bench C · property imagery

Revealing a representative photograph

Left is production: the photograph replaces flat grey in whichever frame it finishes decoding. Right is the concept. The constraint that shapes all four: the source data labels every one of its 347 photographs representative, so the caption is in the first frame of the reveal, never added after it.

clip-path and opacity only · no scale, no crop, no distortion

And the third of the register that has no photograph at all

121 of the 347 available records — 35% — name an image file that is not in assets/project-images/, the generic commercial.jpg, builder-floor.jpg, villa.jpg and apartment.jpg fallbacks among them. Production sets the URL as a background image with no error path, so those tiles are flat grey with a badge claiming a representative photograph sits on them. No reveal fixes this; a designed absence does.

Bench D · architectural ornament

Is the ornament worth its weight?

Two candidates for interaction opportunity F, side by side with their real cost. The SVG datum field is 14 elements and responds to the pointer. The canvas sun study is a per-frame raking-light field of the kind the brand document already permits. Both are measured below rather than asserted.

14 nodes · 0 frames drawn · responds to pointer only

Verification protocol

What is published, and what still has to be confirmed.

Of the 347 available references, 287 were recently re-verified and 60 carry availability still to be confirmed. The ornament behind this text must not make either number harder to read.
